newsitem.title: USA: Skater Baiul tells Oprah she drank before driving.
newsitem.headline: Skater Baiul tells Oprah she drank before driving.

text.p: Olympic figure skating champion Oksana Baiul said on Friday that she had four or five drinks before crashing her car last month in Bloomfield, Connecticut.
But Baiul, who appeared on Friday's Oprah Winfrey show, suggested that she was not drunk despite having the drinks, called Long Island iced teas, which contain a mixture of several liquors.

The 19-year-old Ukrainian skater was admitted into an alcohol education programme on Feb. 4 in a plea-bargain on drunk driving charges. She was also fined the maximum $90 plus costs on a separate charge of driving too fast for conditions.
Baiul, who lives in Simsbury, Connecticut, was originally charged with driving while intoxicated and reckless driving after she ran her Mercedes off a road and crashed on Jan. 12.
On the programme, Winfrey asked: "How many drinks had you had?"
"I think a lot," said Baiul. "I think I would say ... four or five, yeah ... I was drinking Long Island iced tea."
"You had to be drunk if you had four Long Island iced teas," Winfrey said.

Baiul, who is two years below Connecticut's legal drinking age, had a blood alcohol content of 0.168 percent at the time of the accident, according to a hospital report made public. The state's legal limit for adults is 0.10 percent.
Under Connecticut law, the case will be expunged from her record when she completes the alcohol education programme.
